heading.en: Do not waste half the wave

hook.en: A half-wave *rectifier* throws away every negative half cycle. With a centre-tapped transformer and one more diode, we can use both halves.

title.en: Explain the working of a centre-tap full-wave rectifier
State its ripple factor, efficiency and PIV

say.en: A half-wave rectifier throws away every negative half cycle. With a centre-tapped transformer and one more diode, we can use both halves. In this lesson: Explain the working of a centre-tap full-wave rectifier.
Use V dc equals 2V m/ pi and I rms equals I m/ the square root of 2.
State its ripple factor, efficiency and PIV.

body.en: The secondary of the transformer has a centre tap (CT) that acts as the common return. The two ends feed diodes D1 and D2, whose cathodes are joined to one end of the load; the other end of the load goes to the centre tap. In the positive half cycle D1 conducts and D2 is off; in the negative half D2 conducts and D1 is off. Both drive current through the load in the same direction, so the output has two pulses per cycle and the ripple frequency is twice the supply frequency.

points.en: D1 and D2 conduct in alternate half cycles
Ripple frequency = 2f (100 Hz for 50 Hz mains)

narration.en: In a centre-tap full-wave rectifier, D1 conducts in one half cycle and D2 in the other, both sending current through the load the same way. The output has two pulses every cycle.
narration.kn: ಮಧ್ಯ-ಟ್ಯಾಪ್ ಪೂರ್ಣ-ತರಂಗ ದಿಷ್ಟಕಾರಿಯಲ್ಲಿ D1 ಒಂದು ಅರ್ಧ ಚಕ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ, D2 ಇನ್ನೊಂದರಲ್ಲಿ ವಹಿಸುತ್ತವೆ; ಎರಡೂ ಲೋಡ್ ಮೂಲಕ ಒಂದೇ ದಿಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಕಳುಹಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

say.en: D1 and D2 conduct in alternate half cycles.
Ripple frequency equals 2f (100 hertz for 50 hertz mains).
The secondary has a centre tap. Two diodes go to the ends; the load goes between their joined cathodes and the centre tap.
In the positive half D1 conducts; in the negative half D2 conducts. Both send current through the load in the same direction.
So the output has two pulses every cycle. The ripple frequency is twice the mains frequency: 100 hertz.
The d.c. output doubles to 2 V m by pi, efficiency rises to 81.2 percent, but each diode must stand twice V m.

body.en: With V_m the peak of each half of the secondary: $V_{dc} = 2V_m/\pi \approx 0.636V_m$, $I_{dc} = 2I_m/\pi$ and $I_{rms} = I_m/\sqrt{2}$. The ripple factor falls to 0.482 and the maximum efficiency rises to 81.2 %. The drawbacks: each diode must withstand a PIV of 2V_m, and the centre-tapped transformer is bulkier (TUF ≈ 0.693).

narration.en: The full-wave rectifier doubles the d.c. output to 2 V m by pi, cuts the ripple factor to 0.482 and doubles the efficiency to 81.2 percent. But each diode must stand 2 V m.
narration.kn: ಪೂರ್ಣ-ತರಂಗ ದಿಷ್ಟಕಾರಿ ನೇರ ಔಟ್‌ಪುಟ್ ಅನ್ನು 2Vm/π ಗೆ ದ್ವಿಗುಣಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, ತರಂಗಾಂಶ ಅಂಶ 0.482, ದಕ್ಷತೆ 81.2 ಶೇಕಡಾ. ಆದರೆ ಪ್ರತಿ ಡಯೋಡ್ 2Vm ತಡೆಯಬೇಕು.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A 12-0-12 volts r.m.s. transformer feeds a centre-tap full-wave rectifier with a 1 k ohms load ideal diodes. Find V dc, I dc, the ripple frequency 50 hertz mains and the PIV of each diode.
V m each half equals 12 the square root of 2 is approximately 16.97 volts.
V dc equals 2V m/ pi equals 2 times 16.97 over 3.1416 is approximately 10.8 volts; I dc equals 10.8 milliamperes.
Ripple frequency equals 2 times 50 equals 100 hertz.
PIV equals 2V m is approximately 33.9 volts.
So the answer is V dc is approximately 10.8 volts, I dc is approximately 10.8 milliamperes, 100 hertz, PIV is approximately 33.9 volts.

body.en: Going from half-wave to full-wave doubles the d.c. (0.318 → 0.636 V_m), doubles the efficiency (40.6 → 81.2 %), doubles the ripple frequency (f → 2f) and, for the centre-tap circuit, doubles the PIV (V_m → 2V_m). Only the ripple factor drops (1.21 → 0.482).
